recap.text: Down in the channel, one of the two Mongo automatons explodes on the third rail, and the other hauls the Gore-Gore corpse up against the wall. Carl loots the body and takes 498 gold, an Ochre Line Engineer's Key, a bottle of Rev-Up Magic Hair Restoration, and the neighborhood map. The map fills his interface with the whole Ochre line, every stop and the position of every train.

Louis sets Carl down, and Carl finds his hair burned off, eyebrows included, though his skin has healed. Donut says he looks like a crest guy going as one for Halloween and refuses a sidekick with no eyebrows. Carl answers that he has a potion to grow it back, Rev-up hair tonic, which the mantaurs dropped on the fourth floor, though he hears the results run a little overenthusiastic.

Carl stares at the Rev-up Magic Hair Restoration Tonic and its really, really long pamphlet, and after a fifth reading he waits for Katia. She mixes the eyebrows, eyelashes and head, and Splash Zone's water spell will not cast in the saferoom, so Carl runs to the shower and comes out with hair to his waist. The Celestial hairbrush from Club Vanquisher gives twenty-five percent to Constitution, so he must keep it long.

beats.headline: Off Gore-Gore
beats.text: Down in the channel, one of the two Mongo automatons explodes on the third rail, and the other hauls the Gore-Gore corpse up against the wall. Carl loots him: 498 gold and three items. An Ochre Line Engineer's Key, a bottle of Rev-Up Magic Hair Restoration, and the neighborhood map, which fills his interface with the whole Ochre line, every stop and the position of every train.
beats.gist: Down on the tracks, Carl loots the Gore-Gore corpse and takes a bottle of Rev-Up Magic Hair Restoration.

beats.headline: No eyebrows
beats.text: Louis puts Carl down, and Carl puts a hand to his head. His skin has healed, but his hair is gone, burned off, and his eyebrows too. Donut says he looks like he is going as one of those crest guys for Halloween, and she will not have a sidekick with no eyebrows. It's okay, Carl says: he has a potion that grows it back, Rev-up hair tonic. The mantaurs dropped them on the fourth floor, but from what he hears the results are a little overenthusiastic.
beats.gist: Carl's burned-off hair and eyebrows can be regrown by Rev-up hair tonic, though the results run overenthusiastic.

beats.headline: Waiting for Katia
beats.text: Carl stares at the bottle. The set comes with little plastic gloves, cotton swabs and a fold-out instruction pamphlet that is really, really long. Donut fusses that the number one crawler simply cannot be without eyebrows. His view counter has spiked, which tells him this has to be some sort of trap. Mordecai insists it works if he follows the instructions to a T, but they are convoluted, full of warnings against letting it touch anywhere you do not want hair, so after a fifth reading Carl waits for Katia.
beats.gist: Carl stares at the hair tonic, reads its long warnings five times, and waits for Katia.

beats.headline: Uh-oh
beats.text: Katia reads the instructions and mixes in little plastic trays, an extra set of hands holding Carl's head still: eyebrows first, then the eyelashes, a mix almost identical to the pubic hair recipe. For the head she mixes in the large tray and sends Louis for Splash Zone; a splotch lands on the table, and its rock-like surface sprouts hair. Then she splotches the cold tonic on and counts down from five. Uh-oh, says Splash Zone: his water spell counts as offensive and will not cast in the saferoom. Carl runs to the shower, because the tonic adds length for as long as it stays on, and comes out with hair to his waist that grows back when cut. About two weeks, Mordecai says.
beats.gist: Katia mixes the tonic, Splash Zone's water spell fails, and Carl runs to the shower with waist-length hair.

beats.headline: Now it stays long
beats.text: Carl's Celestial item from the fight at Club Vanquisher is a hairbrush whose benefits include twenty-five percent to Constitution, and hair that will be shiny and healthy and goddamn glisten. That boost alone makes the brush frustratingly invaluable; like his boxers, it is now too good to give up. Carl had been planning on cutting his hair after the tonic's regrowth effect finally ebbed. Now he will have to keep it long.
beats.gist: Carl keeps his hair long because the brush's twenty-five percent Constitution boost is too good to give up.
